quote: 1. To compound your money, and not your mistakes, your goal is to buy on the way up—not on the way down.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 2. If you don't feel like a fool, you're not managing risk.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 3. You must have a love for the market in order to be successful in this game.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 4. Do not invest in the present. The present is not what moves stock prices.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 5. Long-term success in the stock market has nothing to do with hope or luck. Winning stock traders have rules and a well-thought-out plan. Conversely, losers lack rules, or if they have rules, they don't stick to them for very long; they deviate.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 6. I cut the losers very quickly. The maximum loss I allow is 7%.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 7. My results went from average to stellar when I finally made the choice that I was going to make every trade an intelligent risk/reward decision.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 8. It was all because I got emotional and dropped every tool of discipline I've ever had.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 9. When you tell yourself, I'm going to break my rule just this one time, you open the door to losing discipline, because it's never just 'one time.'
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 10. I've always loved to play games, and face it: investing is one big game. You need to be decisive, open-minded, flexible and competitive.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 11. Chart patterns are not the cause; they're the effect. Human behavior hasn't changed and isn't likely to change much in the future.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 12. You can tell a lot by volume. If the volume doubles one day and the stock moves to a new high, it is telling you a lot of people are interested in the stock and buying it.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 13. I believe that good investors are successful not because of their IQ, but because they have an investing discipline. But, what is more disciplined than a machine? A well-researched machine can make many average investors redundant, leaving behind only the really good human investors with exceptional intuition and skill.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 14. The best risk control is knowing what you are doing.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 15. You don't have to involve yourself in every market movement. In fact, you should not attempt to. Be an exacting opportunist. Be selective and pick your entry spots very carefully. Wait until the probabilities are stacked in your favor before you act.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 16. The first thing I do is figure out how much money I could lose.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 17. I like putting all my eggs in one basket and then watching the basket very carefully.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 18. If you want to be the best, you have to do things that other people are unwilling to do.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 19. There really is no intelligent reason to increase your trading size if your positions are showing losses.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 20. I study the market because I want to do it and because I'm fascinated to find out what makes the stock go up and what is going to be the next big winning stock.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 21. Concentrating your bets decreases your overall risk because where you tend to be in trouble is if you have 35 or 40 names. If you have a big massive position, it has your attention.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 22. Do your homework. Recap the day. What do I want to happen tomorrow? What happens if the opposite occurs? What happens if nothing happens? Think through all the 'what-ifs.' Anticipate and plan, rather than react.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 23. Soros's great gift was how to use leverage, and how much money to have down based on the risk/reward and your sense of conviction.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 24. The more disciplined you can get, the better you are going to do in the market.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 25. I put a lot more weight into how this stock is acting relative to the S&P — you can see real divergences when stocks are making new highs and the relative strength line is not.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 26. Practice does not make perfect. Only perfect practice makes perfect.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 27. With every trade I make, my approach is always 'risk-first.' By thinking and acting 'risk-first,' you know exactly what you stand to lose if you're wrong, which in trading is far more important than what you stand to gain if you're right, because if you lose all your chips, the game is over.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 28. You want some institutional ownership, because they really power a stock higher, but you don't want too much sponsorship. I would say 1% to 20% is the ideal range.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 29. My goal is not to buy at the lowest or cheapest price but at the 'right' price, just as a stock is ready to move significantly higher. Trying to pick a bottom is unnecessary and a waste of time; it misses the whole point.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 30. I've also never hung onto a security if the reason I bought it has changed. That's when you need to sell.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 31. Therefore, you want to cut your losses quickly.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 32. It takes courage to ride a profit with huge leverage.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 33. Once the relative strength starts falling off, I usually get out of the stock.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 34. Governments defending prices against fundamentals always lose.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 35. You can make money or you can make excuses. But you can't make both.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 36. If you try to learn from every single trade that you make, you are only going to get better and better as time goes on.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 37. Once you make a lot of money, it's incredibly enjoyable to give it away. It's a way to satisfy the soul.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 38. Being wrong is acceptable, but staying wrong is totally unacceptable.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 39. I went from mediocre to a stellar performer when I told myself: To heck with worrying about the money and obsessing over the scoreboard. I'm just going to focus on being the best trader I can be and sticking to the rules.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 40. I'm always thinking about losing money as opposed to making money. Don't focus on making money; focus on protecting what you have.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 41. You may feel dumb breaking even on a trade that was once at a profit; however, you'll feel a lot worse if you turn a good-size gain into a loser.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 42. The idea of studying the greatest stocks of all time to see what made them great made a lot of sense to me.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 43. I never try to make money in the stock market. I buy on the assumption that they could close the market the next day and not reopen it for five years.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 44. The mistake I'd say 98% of money managers and individuals make is they feel like they got to be playing in a bunch of stuff. And if you really see it, put all your eggs in one basket and then watch that basket very carefully.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 45. I look at the five-year earnings growth record and the last two quarters of earnings relative to the previous year's levels.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 46. One of the most important things to do is to not play when you don't see a fat pitch.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 47. Everyone has a stop loss. For some, it's when they go broke. Then they take the ultimate stop loss... they quit trading!
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 48. Every time I buy a stock, I write down the reasons why I bought it. Doing this helps cement in my mind the characteristics of a winning stock. Maybe even more important, it helps me learn from my mistakes.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 49. I never use valuation to time the market. I use liquidity considerations and technical analysis for timing.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 50. What I learned was sizing is 70 or 80% of the equation. It's not whether you're right or wrong. It's about how much you make when you're right and how much you lose when you're wrong.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 51. You're the manager, and it's up to you to protect your hard-earned capital.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 52. It's amazing how well you can do if you start compounding your money. If you start getting some very nice returns each year, that small amount of money can really build itself into a very substantial amount.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 53. Growth comes from having the courage to look at the difficult times and dissect what went wrong.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 54. The relative strength is very important. Again, I look for at least above 80, and preferably above 90.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 55. I've thought a lot of things when I'm managing money with great, great conviction, and a lot of times I'm wrong. And when you're betting the ranch and the circumstances change, you have to change, and that's how I've always managed money.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 56. Growth comes at the expense of comfort.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 57. I've never used the stop loss. Not once. It's the dumbest concept I've ever heard.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 58. My longevity stems from the fact that I try to control risk as much as possible. When the market starts down I sell quickly and don't let the losses get out of hand.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 59. The key is to see things as they are—operating in the now—without seeing things as worse than they are out of fear, or better than they are out of greed.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 60. I'm only rich because I know when I'm wrong.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 61. There are only four things in trading that you can control directly: Before you make the trade, you control what you buy, how much you buy, and when you buy. After you make the trade, you control when you sell.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 62. When you re-frame cutting losses and celebrate avoiding a large loss and freeing up capital for a better trade, suddenly having discipline becomes second nature and being undisciplined becomes painful.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 63. None of us have figured out a better way to manage risk, or to avoid a big decline, other than taking a small loss.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 64. Making the decision to cut your loss in a stock requires that you accept the notion that only you can be wrong; the market is never wrong.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 65. My percentage of winners is only about 50/50, because I cut my losers very quickly. The maximum loss I allow is 7%, and usually I am out of a losing stock a lot quicker. I make my money on the few stocks a year that double and triple in price. The profits in those trades easily makes up for all the small losers.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 66. The greatest thing about the market is that it is always fun to be looking for that next big winner— trying to find the stock with all the characteristics that are going to make it have a big move. To me it is like a giant treasure hunt.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 67. Soros has taught me that when you have tremendous conviction on a trade, you have to go for the jugular. It takes courage to be a pig.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 68. I make most of my mistakes if I actually start trading too early — it's amazing how some of these things gap up and then a half an hour later you're already down a couple points.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 69. Everyone makes mistakes; that's unavoidable. But not correcting a mistake or minimizing the damage of a position gone wrong is completely under your own control.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 70. Most of my big mistakes have been selling too early… great companies, I often buy too early, but I don't sell.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 71. Not losing big is the single most important factor for winning big. As a speculator, losing is not a choice, but how much you lose is.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 72. One of the most suicidal things you can do in trading is to keep adding to a losing position.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 73. What exactly are you trying to accomplish? Do you want to make money, or are you engaged in an exercise in ego to prove that, somehow, you know more than the market?
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 74. Amateurs are scared of positions that stop them out once or twice or just weary of the struggle; professionals are objective and dispassionate.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 75. Stocks should be at a profit the first day you buy them. In fact, having a profit on the first day is one of the best indicators that you are going to make money on that trade.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 76. Earnings don't move the overall market; it's the Federal Reserve Board. Focus on the central banks and focus on the movement of liquidity. Most people in the market are looking for earnings and conventional measures. It's liquidity that moves markets.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 77. The moment the price hits the stop-loss, I sell the position without question. Once I'm out of the stock, I can then evaluate the situation with a clear head.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 78. There is a lot more noise and movement in the market with high speed trading and computerized algorithms, but the stocks that have the biggest moves continue to have the same characteristics.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 79. The greatest investors make large concentrated bets where they have a lot of conviction. They're not buying 35 or 40 names and diversifying.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 80. If you are not willing to accept small losses, you will take big losses.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 81. I'm only gonna buy exactly at the buy point, exactly where the stock was coming out into new highs above the majority of the base.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 82. I strongly believe the only way to make long-term returns in our business that are superior is by being a pig.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 83. The way to build superior long-term returns is through preservation of capital and home runs.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 84. You must not risk more than you can reasonably expect to gain; otherwise, you're stacking the odds against you, and that's gambling.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 85. The difference between interest and commitment is the will not to give up. When you truly commit to something, you have no alternative but success.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 86. If you want to reap big gains in the market, make up your mind right now that you are going to separate trading from your ego. It's more important to make money than it is to be right.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 87. I've always made even higher returns in bear markets than bull markets.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 88. Always go in with a plan and approach every trade risk-first.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 89. I've learned many things from George Soros, but perhaps the most significant is that it's not whether you're right or wrong that's important, but how much money you make when you're right and how much you lose when you're wrong.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 90. The single most important advice I can give anybody is: Learn from your mistakes. That is the only way to become a successful trader.
speaker: David Ryan
